chief_complaint: painful deep cystic pimples on face and back
hpi_details: A 26-year-old female presents to the clinic with painful deep cystic pimples on face and back. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: She thinks the deep, painful lumps on her face and back are cystic boils triggered by a hormonal surge from recent stress and eating too much dairy.
concerns: She is worried that the deep throbbing lumps will leave permanent pitted scars across her face before her sister's wedding in two months.
expectations: She hopes to get a prescription for oral medication or antibiotics because over-the-counter face washes have not touched the deep swelling.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Nodular Acne is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Nodular Acne: Oral Doxycycline, topical retinoids, discuss Isotretinoin, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.

dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.

boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.

reference_soap.subjective:
Chief Complaint: painful deep cystic pimples on face and back

A 26-year-old female presents with painful, deep cystic nodules involving the face and back that have been progressively worsening.
reference_soap.objective: Multiple deep-seated, tender erythematous nodules and cysts with scattered comedones over the face, chest, and back. Post-inflammatory scarring noted in areas of resolved lesions.
reference_soap.plan: Assess pregnancy status and intentions before doxycycline or topical retinoids; avoid these medicines during pregnancy. Use combination acne therapy as appropriate, limiting oral-antibiotic duration and pairing it with benzoyl peroxide. Consider isotretinoin for severe or refractory disease with its required pregnancy-prevention program and monitoring. Refer to Dermatology for extensive scarring or treatment failure.

teaching.one_liner: A severe inflammatory form of acne with deep, painful cysts and nodules on the face and back.

must_ask.say: How deep and painful are the pimples?
Where is the acne — face, back?
How long has this been going on?

history.answer: I came in because I've been getting these really painful, deep pimples on my face and back, and they keep getting worse.
They started appearing about two months ago, and over the past several weeks they have become much larger, deeper, and more swollen.
They are mostly on my cheeks, along my jawline, across my upper back, and a few on my chest.
They feel like large, firm, tender bumps and cysts trapped deep under the skin, rather than small surface pimples.
Yes, they throb and hurt quite a bit whenever I touch my face or lean back in a chair, though they do not itch.
No, they don't fade away after a few hours; once a lump forms, it stays inflamed for weeks at a time.
I had mild teenage blemishes on my forehead years ago, but I have never experienced severe, painful lumps like this before.
I tried over-the-counter salicylic acid face washes and benzoyl peroxide cream for a few weeks, but neither helped at all.
Yes, as the older lesions heal, they leave behind dark red marks and small pitted, indented scars that make me very self-conscious.
I have been feeling unusually tired and run-down lately, but I have not had any fevers, chills, or night sweats.
No, I have no blisters, peeling, or ulcers in my mouth, eyes, or genital area.
No, my skin is not peeling off or sloughing, and I do not have any dark purple spots or bruises.
No, my lips, tongue, and throat are fine, and I haven't had any trouble breathing or swallowing.
No, I haven't started any new prescription medications, antibiotics, pain relievers, or supplements.
No, I haven't changed my cosmetics, moisturizers, laundry detergent, or hair products recently.
No, I haven't been bitten by insects, and I haven't gone hiking, camping, or traveling recently.
No, I have no personal history of eczema, asthma, or chronic allergic rhinitis.
No, my joints feel completely normal with no stiffness, and my nails haven't changed at all.
No, I have not tried any prescription steroid ointments or antifungal creams.
I am in a monogamous relationship with my partner, we use barrier protection, and I have never had genital sores or rashes.
I thought maybe my hormones were thrown out of whack from stress and eating dairy, causing these deep under-the-skin boils.
I'm terrified that these deep lumps will leave permanent pitted scars all over my cheeks right before my sister's wedding photos in two months.
I was hoping to get prescribed some strong oral pills or antibiotics, since topical washes haven't done anything to shrink these deep cysts.
I have no chronic medical conditions, and my health has otherwise been good.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been admitted to a hospital.
I don't take any daily prescription medications, over-the-counter pills, or dietary supplements.
I have no known allergies to medications, foods, or latex.
I have never smoked cigarettes, and I only have a glass or two of wine socially on weekends.
I work as an administrative assistant in an office, and I live in an apartment with a roommate.
My father dealt with severe acne when he was young, but no one in my family has autoimmune skin conditions or psoriasis.
My last period started about two weeks ago, and my menstrual cycles are regular every 28 days.
We use condoms consistently, and I am definitely not pregnant, though I hope to start a family in a few years.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 118/74 mmHg, pulse 72 beats/min, respiratory rate 14 breaths/min, temperature 36.6°C, SpO2 99% on room air.
Young adult female appearing tired and distressed regarding her skin, but in no acute cardiopulmonary distress.
Multiple tender, deep-seated erythematous nodules and cysts with open and closed comedones across the face, chest, and upper back, with scattered pitted scars in areas of resolved lesions.
No cervical, submental, or submandibular lymphadenopathy detected.
Oral mucosa is moist and pink without mucosal ulcers, erosions, or mucosal edema.
Conjunctivae are clear without injection or discharge, and sclerae are anicteric.
No peripheral joint swelling, warmth, or tenderness; fingernails and toenails show no pitting, ridging, or onycholysis.
No nodules, sinus tracts, comedones, or ulcers in the axillary, inguinal, or anogenital folds.
